summary: Interpreted the repair-path receipt and answered that question. Receipt 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84 parsed all five events and evaluated the six comparisons: once the restarted node fell behind a leader that had committed ten more entries and snapshotted with TrailingLogs 0, the snapshot install engaged, the node's applied write became majority-write, its minority write disappeared, the conflict index entry was gone from its log and its configuration became {A,B,C,D,E} — all holds at index 4 — while cluster-wide applied consistency stayed violated at the same index because the node that kept up was never sent a snapshot. So the answer is that the library does engage installSnapshot on its own, per node, and that install replaces the divergent entry, the applied state and the stale configuration together; a divergent node that stays up to date with the leader is not repaired by any observed path. The installSnapshot effects were recorded as reusable knowledge with this receipt, the repair question was marked explained with no defect judgment of its own, and the parent and child accounts were revised so their "no repair path exercised" limitation becomes the observed per-node repair scope, with joint histories added across the receipts. Incomplete: the no-feature restart control inside the cluster, the unexercised user Restore and term-changing truncation paths, and whether a divergent node would organically fall behind often enough for the repair to happen.
